votes.motion: Adopt Joint Ceremonial Resolution 09 of 2024 recognizing March 31, 2024 as International Transgender Day of Visibility in Salt Lake City
votes.description: A joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall officially recognizing March 31, 2024 as International Transgender Day of Visibility in Salt Lake City.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and consider adopting on tonight's consent agenda the Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard – Leading City Procurement Reform grant application
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on a grant application from the Division of Purchasing and Contract Management to the Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard and moves the item to the consent agenda for adoption.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 15 of 2024 – Yalecrest–Princeton Heights Local Historic District
votes.description: Closes the public hearing and adopts an ordinance amending the zoning map to apply the H-Historic Overlay District, establishing the Yalecrest-Princeton Heights Local Historic District covering approximately 43 homes along Princeton Avenue.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 16 of 2024 – Rezone at Approximately 756 South Montgomery Street
votes.description: Closes the public hearing and adopts an ordinance rezoning the property at approximately 756 South Montgomery Street from R-1/5,000 to RMF-30 to allow construction of a higher number of residential dwellings.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 17 of 2024 amending the Fiscal Year 2024 final budget of the Salt Lake City Library including the employment staffing document only for items as shown on the motion sheet
votes.description: Closes the public hearing and adopts Library Budget Amendment No. 2 for FY 2023-24, including over $1.3 million in additional funding for the Main Library roof renovation project.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and defer action to a future meeting on the rezone at 2260, 2270, and 2290 East 1300 South
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on the proposed rezone from R-1/7,000 to CB (Community Business District) for properties at 2260, 2270, and 2290 East 1300 South and defers Council action to a future meeting.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 18 of 2024 – Zoning Map and General Plan Amendments at Approximately 2445 South 500 East (Woodland Commons)
votes.description: Adopts an ordinance rezoning properties at approximately 2445 South 500 East from R-1/7,000 to RMF-35 and amending the Sugar House Community Master Plan Future Land Use Map to facilitate construction of eight townhomes.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 19 of 2024 – Rezone and Master Plan Amendment at 803, 805, 807, and 815 West Simondi Avenue and 802, 806, 810, and 814 West 300 North
votes.description: Adopts an ordinance rezoning properties at Simondi Avenue and 300 North from R1/7000 to RMF-30 and amending the Northwest Community Master Plan Future Land Use Map to allow greater flexibility in housing types.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 10 of 2024 authorizing the Salt Lake County Housing Authority (Housing Connect) to operate within Salt Lake City for the development known as the 44 North Apartments including ongoing rental assistance
votes.description: Adopts a resolution declaring a need for Housing Connect to exercise its powers within Salt Lake City, enabling it to partner with First Step House to develop 67 affordable apartments at 44 and 48 North 1000 West for tenants earning 25%–35% of area median income.

votes.motion: Initiate a legislative action starting the process for City staff to research and draft an ordinance that would create a Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) program for the Sugar House Business zoning districts
votes.description: Directs City staff to research and draft an ordinance establishing a TDR program for Sugar House Business zoning districts to foster sustainable urban growth while safeguarding historical and cultural assets.

Approves multiple consent items including setting public hearing dates for zoning amendments, a street closure ordinance, a grant application approval for Bloomberg Center for Cities at Harvard, and a board appointment for Kristen Lavelett to the Business Advisory Board.
